label: 1 Peter is addressed to Christians in the province of Bithynia

place.note: The address names the province of Bithynia, on the southern Black Sea coast. Pinned to the Bithynia province resource (991389). Pliny (lit-pliny-pontus-bithynia) governed Bithynia together with Pontus and gives the second attestation c. 111–113.

date.note: Composition of 1 Peter. Traditional Petrine authorship puts it before Peter's death under Nero (c. 64); the majority view holds it pseudonymous, c. 70–90. Harnack (p. 186 n.) assigns it to 'the earlier years of Domitian' (c. 81–85). Upper bound 96 (end of Domitian); a minority dates it into the early second century.

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, pp. 92–93 (register of communities traceable before Trajan), 186

notes: Harnack's register lists 'a number of churches in Bithynia and Pontus (1 Pet. i. 1; Pliny's ep. to Trajan).' 1 Peter and Pliny are the two independent witnesses to the province: 1 Peter (c. 80s) then Pliny (c. 112).
